subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these travel-expense records.

judge.implied_focus: Characterizing the nature and cost profile of asset/expense purchases (what was bought, its category, cost tier, and deployment scope)

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: Flags travel relevance, but the query is explicitly about TRAVEL-expense records, so this is near-tautological and points away from the asset-purchasing focus the other columns build.

per_column.name: expense_purpose
per_column.rationale: Classifies the purpose/nature of the expense, a core facet of a spend-characterization focus.

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Details what asset was acquired, a coherent attribute of the purchasing focus.

per_column.name: deployment_scope
per_column.rationale: Describes who/what the spend serves, a sensible facet of the asset/spend structure.

per_column.name: asset_cost_tier
per_column.rationale: Buckets cost magnitude, directly supporting a cost-profile focus.

per_column.name: processing_delay
per_column.rationale: Operational latency metric orthogonal to the asset/cost characterization; a scattered addition.

judge.rationale: Four of six columns (expense_purpose, asset_category, deployment_scope, asset_cost_tier) cohere around a single inferable focus: characterizing what was purchased and its cost/deployment profile. However coherence is undercut in two ways. First, the framing is oddly divorced from the stated domain: these are 'travel-expense records,' yet the inferred purpose/asset categories are dominated by hardware/laptops/cloud, and 'is_travel_related' being mostly false plus 'processing_delay' pull toward different concepts, making the set feel partly like a grab-bag. Second, expense_purpose and asset_category overlap heavily (shared values like travel_equipment, software_service), so the structure has redundant facets rather than cleanly differentiated ones. The implied focus is actionable — an analyst could segment spend by category/cost tier — but the plausible internal inconsistency and the two off-focus columns keep all three scores at a moderate, not strong, level.
